newsitem.title: USA: Talbott consults Europe on NATO, Russia.
newsitem.headline: Talbott consults Europe on NATO, Russia.

text.p: Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbott will discuss NATO expansion plans and efforts to forge a new alliance relationship with Russia during a trip to Europe this week, the State Department said on Monday.

Talbott, a central administration policymaker on Russia and NATO, left Washington on Sunday night and was to visit London, Brussels, Paris and Bonn before returning home on Wednesday night, spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
"This is a trip that focuses on U.S.-European relations and on some of the security issues that have been at the forefront of our relationship," he said.
Talbott "will be in the four capitals to discuss with our allies, including with NATO officials ... a broad variety of issues related to the Madrid summit," Burns added.

Leaders of 16 NATO countries are to meet in Madrid on July 8-9 to formally invite some ex-communist countries in eastern Europe to join the Western alliance. Hungary, Poland and the Czech republic are considered the front-runners, but Romania and Slovenia are also being discussed for early admittance.

In addition, alliance officials are trying to negotiate a special charter with Moscow that would ensure Russia does not feel excluded from the new European security structures but is engaged in a close and cooperative relationship with NATO.
